sentence: This project tests whether defects in cells that wrap around small vessels cause too few blood vessels and too much muscle in lungs.
This project studies the long-term health problems and late effects that survivors of childhood cancer face after their cancer and its therapy.
This project tests an immunotherapy that directs natural killer cells to attack ovarian cancer by binding two proteins found on tumor cells.
This project studies how Ilheus virus infects mammalian and mosquito cells.
This project uses Drosophila and genomics techniques to find genetic variation in genome structure and to learn how it affects evolution.
This project uses a genetic screening method to find out how Mycobacterium tuberculosis acquires nutrients from human macrophages during infection.
This project uses deep learning to build measures that show the risk of dementia in older adults.
This project studies a parasite gene that lets Plasmodium falciparum adapt to sickle-trait red blood cells and may cause disease.
This project uses behavioral, electrophysiological, neuroimaging, and brain manipulation techniques to study the mechanisms behind social competence.
This project builds a cloud-based artificial intelligence platform that gives 4D hemodynamic output from routine anatomic images of the chest.
This project builds a peptide-based hydrogel that delivers four immunotherapy agents in a controlled sequence to help the immune system kill tumors.
This project grows brain organoids from engineered stem cells with and without toxic chemicals to test how chemical exposure affects development.
This project looks for factors that matter in the development of gastric cancer.
This project uses quantitative mass spectrometry to map how signaling networks and proteins work in T cells.
This project studies how premature senescence-triggered vascular diseases lead to cardiovascular dysfunction and atherosclerosis.
This project builds sequencing and computer methods to study how hepatitis B virus varies and avoids the immune response in people with HIV.
This project builds computational tools that learn a patient's genetic ancestry from tumor molecular data without needing the patient's cancer-free DNA.
This project offers statistical analysis and computational biology support to researchers who study HIV.
This project studies how macrophages in tumors make bladder cancer resist current therapies and block immunogenic cancer cell death.
This project studies how the yeast Candida albicans lives in the mouse digestive tract without causing symptoms and sometimes turns into an invasive pathogen.
